failures.title: Renault K4M Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Exhaust Camshaft Lobe Wear - 2000-2015
items.whatHappens: The K4M is known for premature wear on the exhaust camshaft lobes, particularly in earlier non-VVT variants. This manifests as a tapping noise from the top of the engine, rough idling, and a gradual loss of power as valve lift is reduced.
items.repairVsReplace: A standalone camshaft and follower replacement is possible but labour-intensive due to the need to remove the cylinder head. If the wear has caused severe valve damage or the block is otherwise tired, a full Renault K4M replacement is the more reliable route.

items.title: Ignition Coil and Coolant Leak Issues - 2000-2015
items.whatHappens: Ignition coil failure is a frequent cause of misfires and rough running on the K4M. Additionally, coolant leaks can develop from the water pump housing or thermostat, potentially leading to overheating if not addressed promptly.
items.repairVsReplace: These are routine maintenance items. Replacing the ignition coils or sealing a minor coolant leak is highly cost-effective and rarely justifies a full engine replacement unless severe overheating has warped the cylinder head.

failures.goodYearsLine: The K4M is generally considered a robust and simple naturally aspirated unit. Later VVT-equipped variants (such as the K4M 848) saw minor revisions to the valvetrain, making them slightly less prone to the early camshaft wear patterns .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the K4M
variants.intro: The K4M is a Specific engine code, but it is frequently confused with its siblings: the older 8-valve K7M, the newer 1.6L H4M hybrid, and the 1.3L H4Jt turbo. The K4M was the dominant 16-valve naturally aspirated 1.6L tune produced between 2000 and 2015. Where to find the code: The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, typically near the bell housing or on the cylinder head. It is also listed on your vehicle's V5C registration document under "Engine Capacity/Code" or can be decoded from your VIN.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement K4M - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used K4M is a viable option for older, lower-value host vehicles (e.g., Clio II or Megane II under £2,500), provided the replacement unit has a documented service history and no signs of camshaft wear or overheating. Explore our used engine options with a pre-purchase compression test.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: This is the most recommended route for the K4M. A proper reconditioned unit will address the common high-mileage wear points, including a refreshed valvetrain, new water pump, and updated gaskets, restoring the engine to near-factory reliability. View our reconditioned engine services .

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified if your original K4M block has suffered catastrophic overheating damage or severe valvetrain failure. It allows for the installation of upgraded components during the strip-down. Learn more from our rebuilt engine specialists .

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing through our network ensures your K4M is matched correctly, comes with a minimum 12-month warranty, and can be installed by vetted specialists nationwide via our supply and fit network .
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The K4M is commonly found in Renault models with typical UK values ranging from £1,000 to £6,000. Because a reconditioned Renault K4M replacement can cost upwards of £1,290 fitted, it may represent 40-80% of the vehicle's value on older examples. If the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value before committing.

items.question: How much does a Renault K4M engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Renault K4M engine typically costs between £900 and £1,800 for supply only, or £1,290 to £2,320 fully fitted by an independent specialist . Used units start around £350-£800 but require careful inspection for camshaft wear. Full rebuilds addressing valvetrain and cooling issues range from £1,500-£2,500. Labour typically takes 6-8 hours at standard independent rates.

items.question: What is the most common problem with the K4M engine?
items.answer: The most documented issue with the K4M is premature wear on the exhaust camshaft lobes, particularly on earlier non-VVT variants. This wear typically presents as a tapping noise from the top of the engine and a gradual loss of power. Ignition coil failures and minor coolant leaks from the thermostat housing are also frequent but easily resolved. While not usually catastrophic, severe camshaft wear requires a cylinder head strip-down or full engine replacement.

items.question: Which Renault models use the K4M engine?
items.answer: The K4M was Renault's high-volume 1.6-litre 16V petrol engine, fitted to a wide range of models between 2000 and 2015. It is most commonly found in the Clio (II and III), Megane (II and III), and Scenic (II and III). It was also used in the Modus, Dacia Logan, and Dacia Sandero. Always verify your V5C, as the 8-valve K7M or newer H4M are not direct plug-and-play swaps.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned K4M engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned K4M is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the known risk of exhaust camshaft lobe wear at higher mileages. A proper reconditioned unit will feature a refreshed valvetrain, new water pump, and updated gaskets. A used engine is only viable for very low-value host vehicles if it has documented proof of recent camshaft and follower inspection or replacement.

items.question: Is the Renault K4M the same as the K7M?
items.answer: No, while both are 1.6-litre engines from the same Renault K-family, the K4M is a 16-valve DOHC design and the K7M is an older 8-valve SOHC design. They have completely different cylinder heads, camshaft setups, and ECU mappings. They are not physically interchangeable without major modifications to the engine bay and wiring loom.
